bank.prompt: Brisbane's Old Windmill was built on a hilltop in 1828 to grind grain. Why did convicts end up powering a treadmill inside it?

options.label: The hilltop location was too windless to turn the sails
The sails were destroyed in a storm soon after opening

bank.reveal: Poorly sited in a windless spot, the mill's sails couldn't turn. Convicts were forced to work a treadmill — sometimes in leg irons for 14 hours — to keep the millstones grinding.

source.title: Old Windmill Tower | State Library of Queensland
source.verifierNote: Page states it 'is located in a somewhat windless location, it quickly became a place of punishment, with convicts being put to work on a treadmill to keep the arms and heavy millstone turning.'

bank.prompt: After World Expo '88 closed, what was originally planned for Brisbane's iconic Skyneedle tower?

options.label: Relocation to Tokyo Disneyland
Permanent installation at South Bank Parklands

bank.reveal: The 88 m Skyneedle was earmarked for Tokyo Disneyland after Expo closed. Brisbane hairdresser Stefan Ackerie bought it instead and moved it to his South Brisbane HQ, keeping it in the city.

source.title: Expo 88 Skyneedle, sculpture | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states the Skyneedle was purchased by Steve Ackerie who moved it from Southbank to his Stefan corporate HQ; separate source (QSA blog) confirms it was originally planned for Tokyo Disneyland.

bank.prompt: In late 19th-century New Farm, which streets were described as home to 'the well-to-do'?

Flat streets close to the tramway

bank.prompt: The heritage cottages at Cairns Street, Kangaroo Point were built in the 1880s as what type of housing?

Owner-occupier family homes

bank.prompt: Which came first — the formation of the Greater Brisbane Council, or the opening of Brisbane City Hall?

options.label: The formation of the Greater Brisbane Council
The opening of Brisbane City Hall

bank.reveal: Greater Brisbane Council was formed on 1 October 1925 when 20 local authorities amalgamated. City Hall didn't open until April 1930 — five years later.

source.verifierNote: Page states 'On 1 October 1925, the greater Brisbane Council came into effect' and 'Council started meeting in the Brisbane City Hall in 1928 while construction was being completed, before opening in April 1930.'

bank.prompt: The Brisbane suburb of Albion takes its name from a hotel built in 1864. What inspired the hotel's name?

options.label: White quarry walls that reminded the owner of England's white cliffs
A famous inn of the same name in London's East End

bank.reveal: The original Albion Hotel's owner, Tom Haselden, saw the white stone quarry walls nearby and was reminded of the white cliffs of Dover — so the suburb inherited a name rooted in a local landmark.

source.title: Albion Hotel | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'The suburb of Albion was named after the hotel' and that Haselden named it because 'the white walls of the stone quarry in the area reminded him of the white cliffs of Dover.'

bank.prompt: Brisbane's inner suburb of Kelvin Grove gets its name from a house built in the 1860s. Where did the house's owner get the name 'Kelvin Grove'?

options.label: A park in Glasgow, Scotland
A river valley in the English Lake District

bank.reveal: Dr Joseph Bancroft arrived in Brisbane in 1864 and built a home near Enoggera Creek, naming it after Kelvin Grove Park in Glasgow, which he remembered fondly. The suburb took its name from his house.

source.title: Queensland Place Histories - Kelvin Grove
source.verifierNote: Page states the suburb's name 'derives from the 1868 purchase by Joseph Bancroft of land in the area and on which he built a residence called Kelvin Grove Park. It is believed that he named the property after Kelvin Grove Park in Glasgow.'
